content: The test image shows a young soybean seedling with a brownish lesion/canker at a node near the soil line, with grayish stem coloration that could be fungal or normal pubescence. Key candidates: Rhizoctonia (dry reddish-brown canker at soil line), Pythium (water-soaked soft rot), or White_Mold (fluffy white mycelium at nodes).

The reference images for Rhizoctonia show reddish-brown sunken cankers at the soil line/hypocotyl, which matches well with what I see in the test image — a brownish lesion at the node/base of the stem on a young seedling, with the plant showing early signs of damping off near soil level.

The test image shows:
- Young seedling at soil level
- Brownish discoloration/lesion at the stem node near soil line
- Gray coloration consistent with normal stem pubescence mixed with fungal activity
- Dry, firm-looking canker (not water-soaked like Pythium)

This matches Rhizoctonia's characteristic reddish-brown, sunken, dry canker on the lower stem/hypocotyl at the soil line.
